name: Property tax, general operating
plain_description: Tax on the assessed value of real estate and business personal property that pays for general city services (current-year collections, plus small special assessments).

name: Property tax, dedicated to police and fire
plain_description: Property tax millages voted by residents that can only be spent on the police and fire departments (shown as separate millage lines from 2025).

name: Property tax, dedicated to recreation (NORD/NORDC)
plain_description: A 1.5-mill property tax set aside for the city's recreation department (NORD, now NORDC).

name: Property tax, dedicated to parks and parkways
plain_description: A 1.5-mill property tax set aside for the Parks and Parkways department.

name: Property tax, dedicated to streets
plain_description: A 1.9-mill property tax set aside for street maintenance; budgeted at about $7 million a year until about 2019 and almost nothing since.

name: Property tax, back taxes from prior years
plain_description: Property tax collected late, for earlier tax years, on the general (non-dedicated) rolls.

name: Property tax interest and penalties
plain_description: Interest and penalties charged on delinquent property tax bills.

name: Sales and use tax (city share)
plain_description: The city's share of the local sales tax on goods and services, including (from 2025) food and drug sales and the tax on out-of-state online purchases. CAUTION: FY2004-2007 (all books) and FY2008-2013 in books through 2013 print hotel/motel and motor vehicle tax inside this line; use the 'sales-and-related-taxes' rollup for a series that is comparable across all years.

name: Motor vehicle sales tax
plain_description: The city's share of the sales tax on vehicle purchases, printed as 'Motor Vehicle Tax'.

name: Hotel and motel tax
plain_description: Tax paid by visitors on hotel and motel room stays in New Orleans.

name: Utility tax
plain_description: Tax on electricity and gas bills of customers in the city (Entergy New Orleans).

name: Parking tax
plain_description: Tax on parking charged at garages and lots in the city.

name: Document transaction tax
plain_description: Tax paid when property deeds, mortgages and similar documents are recorded.

name: Other small taxes
plain_description: Smaller taxes lumped together: beer, wine and liquor, chain stores, racing and slot machines, airport, sports wagering, Sewerage and Water Board tax, and tax-collection costs.

name: Franchise fees (electric, cable, telephone, wireless)
plain_description: What utilities such as Entergy New Orleans, cable and telephone companies pay the city for the right to use public streets and rights-of-way.

name: Building permits
plain_description: Fees for building permits, demolition permits and use-and-occupancy certificates.

name: Occupational and business licenses
plain_description: Annual licenses that businesses and professionals must buy to operate in the city, including the insurance premium license tax.

name: Alcoholic beverage permits
plain_description: Fees for permits to sell alcohol in bars, restaurants and stores.

name: Taxi, tour guide and ride-hail licenses
plain_description: Permits and fees for taxis, tour guides and operators, and ride-hail (Uber/Lyft-type) companies.

name: Short-term rental permits
plain_description: Permit fees on Airbnb-style short-term rentals; only printed separately from the 2025 books (earlier years sit inside 'licenses-permits-other').

name: Motor vehicle permits and brake tags
plain_description: Fees tied to vehicles, mainly the brake-tag inspection stickers.

name: Electrical, mechanical and safety permits
plain_description: Permits and licences for electrical, mechanical, gas and similar trade work and inspections.

name: Other licenses and permits
plain_description: All other permits: street cuts and closures, mayoralty permits (parades, film), signs, historic-district reviews and other small fees.

name: Harrah's casino rent
plain_description: Rent from Harrah's casino on Canal Street; printed as 'Harrah's Rent' under Intergovernmental from the 2021 book, which moved it there from Service Charges (earlier years sit inside 'general-government-charges').

name: State revenue sharing
plain_description: Money the state shares with local governments out of state tax revenue, including amounts dedicated to police and fire.

name: State video poker revenue
plain_description: The city's share of state-licensed video poker proceeds.

name: State Medicaid payments
plain_description: State payments to the city for Medicaid ambulance services (Upper Payment Limit program).

name: Parish transportation fund (roads and transit)
plain_description: State gasoline-tax money returned to the parish for roads and for transit.

name: State supplemental pay for police and fire
plain_description: State payments toward extra pay for police officers and firefighters ($10-14 million a year in 2009-2013); printed as 'State Aid Other' through the 2020 book and as 'State Supplemental Pay' from the 2026 books.

name: Other state and federal aid
plain_description: Smaller aid lines: other state aid, corrections, federal aid, emergency management, GOMESA oil revenue, the Orleans Parish Communication District and the like.

name: Sanitation service charge
plain_description: The garbage collection and curbside recycling fee charged to residents and businesses.

name: Parking meters
plain_description: Coins and app payments collected at the city's parking meters, including temporary meters.

name: Emergency medical (ambulance) fees
plain_description: Fees billed to patients and insurers for EMS ambulance transport; printed separately only from 2025 (earlier books hold it inside 'public-safety-charges').

name: Public safety charges
plain_description: Fees for public safety services, e.g. airport fire protection and police reports; in books before 2025 this single line also contains ambulance fees.

name: General government charges
plain_description: Fees for city administrative services, mainly the 2% fee the city charges other districts for collecting sales tax and the tax collection fees, plus zoning, planning and utility regulatory fees.

name: Harrah's city support payment
plain_description: A separate annual payment from Harrah's casino for city services; printed separately only from 2025 (earlier books hold it inside 'general-government-charges').

name: Indirect cost recoveries
plain_description: Money the General Fund recovers from grants and other funds for the administrative overhead it provides to them.

name: Other service charges
plain_description: Small charges: streets and towing, parks and parkways, state highway maintenance, and a few lines printed under this heading that are state aid.

name: Traffic camera and red-light fines
plain_description: Fines from automated red-light and speed camera tickets.

name: Parking tickets and traffic/municipal court fines
plain_description: Fines paid on parking tickets, traffic violations and municipal court cases; books split these differently (2005-06 print them as one line, and the 2025+ 'Traffic Fines' line has the dollar amounts of the earlier 'Parking Ticket Collections' line), so they are one rev_id.

name: Other fines and forfeits
plain_description: Smaller fines: health-code violations, abandoned vehicle impound fees, administrative adjudication fees and demolition lien penalties.

name: Interest earnings
plain_description: Interest the city earns on cash balances and bond funds.

name: Rents and royalties
plain_description: Rent on city-owned buildings and land, and landfill and parking royalties.

name: Settlement and judgment fund
plain_description: A transfer to cover legal settlements and judgments, printed only in the 2008-2014 books (about $20 million in 2004).

name: Reimbursements and other miscellaneous
plain_description: Catch-all of reimbursements from other agencies, insurance proceeds, asset sales, contributions and one-time receipts (2015 includes a $36 million BP oil-spill settlement).

name: Use of fund balance
plain_description: Savings from earlier years used to balance the budget; the 2012 actual of $195.9 million is not savings but pension-bond refinancing proceeds, and the 2023 figure appears to include one-time American Rescue Plan (ARPA) money.

name: Transfers from other funds
plain_description: Money moved into the General Fund from other city funds.

name: FEMA community disaster loan
plain_description: Federal disaster loan proceeds after Hurricane Katrina (2005-2009).

name: Gulf Opportunity Zone payment
plain_description: Payments tied to the Gulf Opportunity Zone program after Katrina (2006-2009).

name: Other financing and adjustments
plain_description: Other adjustments, HUD Section 108 loan draws and small bond-related transfers.

name: Federal grants
plain_description: Money from federal agencies for specific programs (health, public safety, transportation, disaster recovery), restricted to those uses.

name: State and local grants
plain_description: State and foundation grants for specific programs; the books print these as State Grants, then State and Local Foundation Grants.

name: Housing and Urban Development (HUD) grants
plain_description: Federal housing and community development money such as CDBG and HOME block grants.

name: Local law enforcement grants
plain_description: Small state grants for local police programs from the Governor's office.

name: Self-generated funds
plain_description: Small funds that departments raise themselves and may spend on their own programs.

name: Special revenue and trust funds
plain_description: Dedicated-purpose and trust funds not listed separately; the 2025+ books print this as 'Self Generated, Spc Rev, Trust Funds'.

name: Library funds
plain_description: The library's dedicated property tax millage plus library fines and fees.

name: Downtown Development District
plain_description: A special property tax paid by downtown property owners for district services; dropped out of the budget as 'Exclude from Budget' in 2026.

name: Economic development fund
plain_description: Property tax set aside for economic development projects.

name: Housing improvement (housing trust) fund
plain_description: Property tax set aside to fund neighbourhood housing improvement.

name: New Orleans Regional Business Park
plain_description: Property tax from the Regional Business Park district (2008-2017).

name: Wisner land trust
plain_description: Proceeds of the Wisner land trust, printed under Mayoral Fellows Program until 2024 and as Wisner Fund from 2025.

name: Grants, contributions and fund transfers
plain_description: A budgeted placeholder for grants and contributions the city expects to receive during the year but cannot yet attribute to a program.
